findings.F1: Below a falling cloud the coins rose on average: on the trending grid bars the 26-day forward return was +3.9 % (t 2.49, 353 cases), and the excess over each coin's drift was -1.8 % (t -1.17). The book's short earned its edge against the drift but lost on the total move, which fits the size block's total of -1.86 % per case and the 0.17 Sharpe against holding's 0.59.
findings.F2: Inside the trending regime, the past 26-day return sorts what follows far more than the cloud's slope does. The two lowest quartiles of the past 26-day return had excess 26-day returns of -15.4 % (t -6.4, 24 cases) and -16.5 % (t -3.2, 23 cases); the two highest had +3.4 % and +9.2 % (rank slope 0.37, time-clustered t 1.65 over 13 month-cells). The tested slow-fall gradient split at -0.12 Welch t.
findings.F3: Across all grid bars, a coin's 26-day return scaled by its volatility predicts its next 26 days. The time-clustered rank slope was 0.25 (t 2.42, 299 cases, 24 cells), the bottom tercile ran -0.31 usual moves against +0.19 for the top tercile, and the top tercile beat the bottom in 15 of 16 coins. The unscaled 26-day return gave quintile excesses from -5.9 % (t -3.3) to +10.0 % (t 2.2), Spearman 0.098 (p 0.003, n 897, clustered t 1.92).
findings.F4: The book's loss came from bull years. Its mean daily return was +0.15 % in 2018 while the coins fell 0.35 % a day, and -0.06 % to -0.07 % in 2020, 2023 and 2024 while the coins rose 0.28 % to 0.44 % a day. Trending-grid forward returns were +24 % to +36 % in 2020, 2021 and 2023 (t 3.0 to 4.8).
findings.F5: The longest-held shorts were the only ones that paid. Trades in the top duration quartile, over about 37 days, earned +7.3 % net (348 trades); the shortest two quartiles lost -5.4 % and -9.6 % (372 and 472 trades), out of 1398 shorts with a mean of -3.2 %.
findings.F6: Cloud thickness inside the trending regime does not separate cleanly. The thickest-cloud quartile was followed by +21.2 % excess (t 2.7, 24 cases) against -9 % to -22 % for the others, but the clustered t was only 1.68 over 13 cells, so it cannot be told apart from chance.
findings.F7: Saturday is the strongest day of the week: the cross-coin mean daily return was +0.45 % (t 2.84, 414 days), Saturday beat the other days in 16 of 19 coins and in 7 of 8 years, but no single year exceeds t 1.6. It is a condition with no gradient, so it supports no idea here.

ideas.idea: When a coin closes below a falling Ichimoku cloud, its return over the next 26 days is more negative the more it has already fallen over the past 26 days.
ideas.consequence: A coin that sits below a falling cloud after a steep 26-day drop is a reason to short it, while one below a falling cloud after a flat or rising month is a reason to refuse the short.
ideas.name: deep fall below cloud continues

ideas.idea: A coin's return over the next 26 days is higher the larger its past 26-day return is relative to its own daily volatility over the past 60 days.
ideas.consequence: A coin with a strong volatility-scaled 26-day rise is a reason to hold it long, and one with a strong volatility-scaled 26-day fall is a reason to stay out or go short.
ideas.name: volatility-scaled monthly momentum
